text:
maria: Heads-up — last night we paged twice for kv-cache-miss spikes in eu-west that turned out to be 30s bursts from a job. Operator fatigue rising. Can we rework paging rules so short noisy spikes don't wake people? :sleepy:

ashwin: yep saw that. The spike pattern is very bursty: high increase for <1m then back to normal. Current alert uses 'rate() > X' without a for: duration.

leo: short take: convert these to P2 (ticket) unless they sustain > 3m OR correlate with GPU saturation/queue depth. We should stop paging on single-node pod-level blips.

jane: agreed. Proposal: two-level alerts — cluster-wide severity for pages, node/pod-level for tickets. Cluster-level uses grouped rate and `for: 3m`. Pod-level uses `for: 10m` and routed to #eng-sre-tickets.

maria: sounds reasonable. Can you sketch a Prometheus rule we could use as a starting point?

ashwin: sure — pseudo-rule below. It groups by cluster and only fires if the increase is sustained:```yaml
- alert: KVCacheMissSustained
  expr: increase(kv_cache_miss_total[3m]) > 100
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache"
```

leo: and a pod-level ticket rule:```yaml
- alert: KVCacheMissPodBlip
  expr: increase(kv_cache_miss_total{pod!~"^infra-.*"}[1m]) > 10
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
```

jane: two extra heuristics: 1) add a sliding-derating that reduces alert score during known deployment windows (mute-window label) and 2) dedupe by hashing on model + region so noisy multi-pod churn doesn't produce N pages.

maria: how do we implement dedupe in Alertmanager? I don't want separate pages where it's really the same root cause across pods.

ashwin: in Alertmanager use `group_by: ['cluster', 'model', 'region']` + `group_wait: 30s, group_interval: 10m, repeat_interval: 4h`. Also set `routes` where severity=page -> oncall, severity=ticket -> ticketing-bot.

leo: also add a pre-filter that checks correlated signals: only page if `gpu_utilization > 75` OR `node_cpu_seconds_total` is high OR `node_restarts` increased. That avoids paging for pure KV cache noise.

jane: note on observability side: add a small SLO dashboard panel showing "pages per 24h by fingerprint" so we can catch noisy fingerprints. If one fingerprint causes >3 pages/day, auto-escalate to an owner.

maria: bonus asks — can we run an experiment: for 2 weeks change the rule set (staging first) and route to ticketing for these cases, then measure missed-severity incidents vs pager reduction?

ashwin: yes. I'll push a staged rule in prometheus-staging and create a dashboard for the experiment. Plan:
- week 0: deploy to staging
- week 1-2: roll to prod but route to ticketing only
- week 3: if incident MTTI unchanged and pages down, flip to page on sustained rule

leo: log snippet of the current noisy spike to attach to the experiment ticket:```
2026-02-11T03:42:12Z kv_cache miss +1200/s for node gpu-12
2026-02-11T03:42:40Z back to baseline
```

alert-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0427 — kv-cache burst analysis (assigned: ashwin) :white_check_mark:

jane: thanks — I'll update runbooks and add the fingerprint panel. Also propose a short README for oncall: when to escalate a ticket to pager (sustained >3m OR correlated infra signals).

maria: perfect. Assign follow-ups: ashwin -> rules + staging deploy, jane -> dashboard + runbook edits, leo -> alertmanager grouping config. We'll reconvene after week 2. :+1:

ashwin: putting a PR up today, link once ready.

leo: thx — glancing at the PR now.

maria: closing loop: reduce pages, keep signal for true infra issues. Thanks everyone.
